To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
ESO422G028 is a giant radio source that exhibits both starburst and restarted AGN activity.

1) ESO422 G28 is a giant radio galaxies with a 13 Gyr old stellar population that is also exhibiting a 10 Myr old starburst, 2) the starburst is predominantly located in a region of the galaxy coincident with the restarted jets, 3) the starburst and restarted jets have been likely triggered by the infall of gas from the North, 4) the gas infall rate is 1 3 M yr 1, and
We present the first study of the stellar and gas properties in the giant radio galaxy ESO422 G28.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the spatial distribution and kinematics of the stellar and gaseous components of ESO422G028.
the study of giant radio galaxies, which are rare objects in which the jets from the central supermassive black hole extend to distances of more than 0.5 Mpc.
understanding the physical processes that drive the formation of stars, and how this relates to the evolution of the galaxies that host them.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ESO422-G028 is an excellent example of a galaxy with a complex and dynamic history.
ESO422-G028 is a radio-loud galaxy that is in the process of merging and that the merger is triggering both the nuclear starburst and the nuclear activity.
ESO422-G028 is a galaxy that has been rejuvenated by the accretion of a gas-rich companion.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have discovered a neutral inflow of gas in a restarted giant radio galaxy.
the giant radio galaxy ESO422 G 028 is in a transitional stage between a quiescent and an active phase.
the neutral inflow of gas is the main driver for the recent star formation and the restarted jet.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the stellar and gas properties in ESO422 G027 are not consistent with the standard model of giant radio galaxies.
the star formation and AGN activity in ESO422 G 028 is intimately related, and that the gas inflow is the likely trigger.
the stellar and gas properties are not necessarily aligned with the radio axis, suggesting the radio jet activity is not solely responsible for the star formation.
